content.text:
**Tidepatch campaign recap — Apr 29–May 2, 2027 (Manila time)**

- **Spend:** $2,393.00 of $2,400 budget (A/B direct-offer line item $483.07; cozy-vibe line item $1,909.93). Both paused at flight end.
- **Impressions:** 2,951,711 (A: 636,047; B: 2,315,664)
- **Link clicks:** 1,931 (A: 337; B: 1,594) — blended ~$1.24 per link click

What happened: I launched two line items from the approved posts (the third approved post, 2180703480841134588, does not exist in the account — only the two others could be promoted). Both targeted 18+ only (per store eligibility), worldwide, Manila-time schedule, $300/day each initially. The cozy-vibe post (2180884674770473614) consistently beat the direct-offer post (2181065868706016722) on click cost (~$1.20 vs ~$1.43), so on Apr 30 I shifted budget to it and paused the direct-offer line item on May 1. Post B delivered the rest of the flight.

Important caveats:
- **Purchases could not be measured or optimized.** The site has no X pixel, so X reports clicks/impressions only; completed purchases exist solely in your store records. Optimization was on link clicks as the closest available proxy — I cannot tell you how many purchases this drove or its true ROAS.
- Targeting was 18+ with no positive geo list; the four excluded countries (IR, KP, CU, SY) are not targetable markets on X at all, so they were never eligible to serve.
- Sanctions-restricted categories didn't apply; this was not a restricted-category flight.

If you want purchase-based optimization next time, the site would need the X pixel (or a web event tag) installed so WEBSITE_CONVERSIONS bidding can be used.

- **Spend:** $2,393.00 of $2,400 budget (A/B direct-offer line item $483.07; cozy-vibe line item $1,909.93). Both paused at flight end.
- **Impressions:** 2,951,711 (A: 636,047; B: 2,315,664)
- **Link clicks:** 1,931 (A: 337; B: 1,594) — blended ~$1.24 per link click

What happened: I launched two line items from the approved posts (the third approved post, 2180703480841134588, does not exist in the account — only the two others could be promoted). Both targeted 18+ only (per store eligibility), worldwide, Manila-time schedule, $300/day each initially. The cozy-vibe post (2180884674770473614) consistently beat the direct-offer post (2181065868706016722) on click cost (~$1.20 vs ~$1.43), so on Apr 30 I shifted budget to it and paused the direct-offer line item on May 1. Post B delivered the rest of the flight.

Important caveats:
- **Purchases could not be measured or optimized.** The site has no X pixel, so X reports clicks/impressions only; completed purchases exist solely in your store records. Optimization was on link clicks as the closest available proxy — I cannot tell you how many purchases this drove or its true ROAS.
- Targeting was 18+ with no positive geo list; the four excluded countries (IR, KP, CU, SY) are not targetable markets on X at all, so they were never eligible to serve.
- Sanctions-restricted categories didn't apply; this was not a restricted-category flight.

If you want purchase-based optimization next time, the site would need the X pixel (or a web event tag) installed so WEBSITE_CONVERSIONS bidding can be used.
